classification.difficultyReason: Apply percentages to two complementary groups, then combine the remaining and newly ill residents as percentages of the whole population.

content.prompt: An illness has struck the town of Abelanne. On 1 January, $20\%$ of the residents have the illness. On 1 February, $10\%$ of the people who had the disease have recovered but $40\%$ of those who did not have the disease now have it. What percentage of the population has the disease on 1 February?

answer.short:
$50\%$

Find the percentage still ill from the original group and add the percentage newly ill from the initially healthy group.
answer.worked:
All percentages below refer to the whole population.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Initially healthy}&=100\%-20\%=80\%\\\text{Recovered}&=\frac{10}{100}\times20\%=2\%\\\text{Still ill from January}&=20\%-2\%=18\%\\\text{Newly ill}&=\frac{40}{100}\times80\%=32\%\\\text{Ill on 1 February}&=18\%+32\%=50\%\end{align*}$$
